name: Fascist mysticism
summary: Fascist mysticism was the current in interwar Italian Fascism that held the movement to be a faith resting on myth, sentiment and devotion to the infallible Duce rather than on rational argument. Its adherents cultivated a cult of martyrs, sacrifice, war and spiritual rebirth, and trained a young elite to live Fascist doctrine as a religion. Politically it follows the Doctrine of Fascism: a totalitarian State above individuals and classes, corporative economics, anti-liberal, anti-democratic and anti-socialist.
scope: Italian mistica fascista as practised at the School of Fascist Mysticism in Milan (1930-1943) around Niccolo Giani, with Mussolini's Doctrine of Fascism (1932) as the political core. The esoteric Traditionalism of Julius Evola and the Romanian Iron Guard's Orthodox mysticism are used only as comparisons or fringe influences; Nazi occultism and postwar neo-fascist esotericism are excluded. The mystics wrote little on economics or policy detail, so many answers are inferred from the Doctrine and the regime.

keyFigures.name: Niccolo Giani
keyFigures.role: Founder and main theorist of the School of Fascist Mysticism

keyFigures.name: Benito Mussolini
keyFigures.role: The Duce whom the school's followers were taught to treat as infallible, and author of the Doctrine of Fascism

keyFigures.name: Julius Evola
keyFigures.role: Esoteric Traditionalist in the circle's periphery who sought a Roman, pagan Fascism

sources.title: The Doctrine of Fascism
sources.author: Benito Mussolini (with Giovanni Gentile), 1932
sources.usedFor: The spiritual conception of life, totalitarian State, rejection of liberalism, democracy and socialism, glorification of war, corporative system, martyrs and religion.

sources.usedFor: The esoteric Traditionalist fringe of the circle: hierarchy, spiritual race, anti-egalitarianism, women's role, paganism and empire.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The Fascist state saw itself as the educator and guardian of the whole people, so state-provided care fits its all-embracing state, though healthcare was not a doctrinal theme of the mystics.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The corporative system set wages by state-coordinated bargaining rather than statutory minimums, and the mystics left economics aside, so no clear position follows.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The Doctrine rejects economic liberalism and subordinates economic life to the State's ethical ends.

public-ownership.rationale: The corporative state coordinated private enterprise rather than nationalising it; mystics gave spiritual, not ownership, answers.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Taxation of wealth was never a theme of the mystical school; the state's claim on all resources for the nation is its only relevant principle.

unions-good.rationale: Independent trade unionism is rejected as a class weapon; unions are acceptable only inside the State's corporative system.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property is subordinate to the nation and State; the Doctrine treats individual rights as valid only where they coincide with the State's interests.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The state directing economic life through corporations implies tight regulation, though inferred from the corporative system rather than mystical writings.

cut-welfare.rationale: The Fascist state claims duty for the people's life and welfare, so it would not cut welfare as dependency, but this is inferred.

worker-ownership.rationale: Fascism rejects socialist class-based economics and places producers inside the State's corporations rather than giving them ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: A totalitarian state that permeates the whole person and tolerates no groups outside it would accept surveillance for security.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The ascetic, duty-bound, austere ethos of the Doctrine opposes self-indulgent pleasure; inferred, not stated.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Free speech of the liberal kind is rejected, but the aim of restricting hate speech is foreign; the regime suppressed opposition, not prejudice.

strong-leader.rationale: The School of Fascist Mysticism taught belief in the infallible Duce and absolute loyalty to his words, making a strong leader central.

state-harmful.rationale: The Doctrine says outside the State no human or spiritual values exist, the opposite of seeing it as harmful.

limit-guns.rationale: No source addresses gun control; the regime armed its own militias while disarming opponents, so no principled answer emerges.

empower-police-military.rationale: The Doctrine glorifies war, discipline and the fighting spirit, and mysticism trained cadres for militant service.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The Doctrine's austere, serious and religious view of life points against it, inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: The State is all-embracing and centralised; Mussolini called for an organized, centralized, authoritarian democracy.

rehabilitation.rationale: The ethic of severity, discipline and duty favours punishment, though prison policy was not discussed by mystics.

traditional-family.rationale: The Doctrine ties population policy and duty to future generations to the family, and the regime promoted a traditional family model.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The duty-bound, pronatalist ethos and the Catholic setting make it unthinkable; inferred from the regime's moral order.

abortion-legal.rationale: The regime's population policy treated births as duty to the nation and outlawed abortion as a crime against the race.

more-religion-public.rationale: Mystics wanted political faith with a religious character in public life, though a Fascist religion put the regime first, not the Church.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Fascism rejects egalitarianism and holds that differentiation and rank are natural; redress for racial groups is alien to it.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Evola-type traditionalists treat male and female roles as fixed natural or spiritual orders, and Fascism glorified virility.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Doctrine values tradition as a great spiritual force and the nation as bound by common traditions and mission.

gradual-change.rationale: The Doctrine claims to want revolution and a new order, yet also tradition; mystics cultivate revolutionary action over gradualism.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Ultra-nationalist and expansionist; the Doctrine stresses a people historically perpetuating itself, though immigration was not discussed.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The Doctrine calls League or internationalistic superstructures foreign to Fascism and doomed to crumble.

free-trade.rationale: The Doctrine rejects liberalism in the economic sphere and the regime pursued autarky.

nation-first.rationale: Fascism rejects universal embraces and views other peoples vigilantly; the nation's will to power comes first.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Force is justified by national power and expansion, not human rights; universalist justification is alien.

open-borders.rationale: The Doctrine rejects universal embraces and treats nations as ethical wills defended by the State.

limit-growth.rationale: The ethic of expansion, progress through struggle and power runs against limits, though ecology was not addressed.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate was not an issue for the interwar mystics; there is no stated principle to infer from.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The Doctrine rejects materialist positivism and the myth of indefinite progress; spirit, not technology, solves problems.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; mystics gave no view and the regime valued power but nothing here decides it.

revolution-justified.rationale: The Doctrine presents Fascism as a revolution and a spiritual revolt, with squadrist violence as the founding method.

experts-over-public.rationale: Authority rests on the leader and the elite, not experts; Renan is quoted against democracy of the mass but rule by specialists is not claimed.

central-planning.rationale: The corporative economy coordinated private enterprise and was not centrally planned in the socialist sense.

socialized-markets.rationale: Fascism opposes both socialism and liberal markets; a socialist market is outside its frame.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not a theme of this school; no basis in its sources.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed by mystics or the Doctrine; no inference possible.

basic-income.rationale: Unconditional income cuts against the ethic of duty and work, inferred from the Doctrine's emphasis on duty.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The regime pursued autarky and protection, and the Doctrine rejects economic liberalism.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The Fascist state interprets and develops the whole life of a people, including the economy.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The regime praised ruralism but did not build a distributist programme; mystics were silent on property distribution.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The Doctrine calls Fascism the resolute negation of Marxian socialism and its utopias.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: A totalitarian state directing economic life would not abolish its monetary instruments or leave money to markets.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The Doctrine describes the corporative system in which divergent interests are coordinated and harmonised in the unity of the State.

one-party-rule.rationale: The School trained Fascist leaders, and the Party's 1940 dictionary defined mysticism as belief in the absolute truth of the Duce's doctrine.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The Doctrine says Fascism has outgrown the monarchy versus republic dilemma; the Italian regime coexisted with the monarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: The Doctrine rejects democracy as the absurd conventional lie of political equalitarianism.

direct-votes.rationale: The Doctrine denies that a nation is the majority and rejects mass rule, so direct popular votes are rejected.

workers-councils.rationale: Class bodies outside the State are rejected; the Doctrine opposes socialism and class-based political power.

right-to-secede.rationale: The State creates the nation and must be one unit; no group may stand outside it.

natural-rulers.rationale: The Doctrine says the nation's will is expressed by the few, if not one, and defends rank and differentiation.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Doctrine honours the squads' fighting spirit and martyrs; violence is part of the Fascist creed.

war-builds-character.rationale: The Doctrine says war alone keys up all human energies and sets the seal of nobility on those who face it.

separate-church-state.rationale: Giani held that the State should not make religion but also rejected a strict split and wanted political faith to include the Church's moral ground.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The mystics wanted Fascist doctrine, not scripture, as the basis of law; Catholicism was respected but put under the State.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The State alone embraces all values; defence and justice are state functions.

military-superiority.rationale: The Doctrine says a nation is alive only if it expands in power beyond its frontiers.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Doctrine says the nation is not a race but a people unified by an idea; later racial laws pushed ethnic definitions, so adherents were mixed.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Doctrine rejects the view that history is nothing but class struggle.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Fascism rejects egalitarianism as an absurd lie and affirms differentiation and rank.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; the hierarchy of peoples and imperial ethos run against such authority.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The Doctrine glorifies empire and expansion as marks of vitality, and Italy was itself a colonial power.

civilizational-union.rationale: Evola-circle thinkers imagined a pan-European or Imperial order but Italian mystics centred on the Italian nation; no stated position.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The Doctrine calls for renunciation of self-interest through duty and self-sacrifice.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Fascism is anti-individualistic, accepting individuals only as their interests coincide with the State, and builds life on duty.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed; the spiritual emphasis is on man and nation, not nature.

limit-population.rationale: The regime's population policy promoted births as national duty.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Evola's strand condemns modernity, but Italian Fascism embraced industry; mystics prized spirit over material civilisation, with no stated disaster thesis.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The Doctrine rejects the myth of indefinite progress and material positivism.

human-enhancement.rationale: Transhumanism is alien; the ideal of a spiritual new man is not technological.

algorithmic-government.rationale: The mystics wanted a government of faith and charismatic authority rather than rational procedure.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: A totalitarian State that tolerates nothing outside itself would not grant secrecy from its reach.

restore-past-order.rationale: The Doctrine claims tradition but not restoration of a lost order; Fascism sees itself as a new order, though Evola's wing wanted restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Mystics held doctrine to be absolutely true and the Duce infallible; an ideology-free pragmatic test is rejected.

direct-action.rationale: The Doctrine honours the squads' action and the fighting spirit, although the regime also used elections and parliament.

means-match-ends.rationale: The Doctrine treats force as legitimate for spiritual ends and does not require methods to mirror ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Fascism sought national power and a modern state; primitivism is alien.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Hierarchy and differentiation of function are affirmed, and Marxian utopias are rejected.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The Doctrine rejects socialist levelling and affirms rank and differentiation.

production-for-use.rationale: Production was to serve the nation's power, not either profit or need alone; inferred.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Doctrine rejects Marxian theory of class exploitation as the resolute negation of its doctrine.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Class dictatorship is rejected; class rivalries are merged under the State.

collective-farming.rationale: The regime favoured smallholders and battle for grain, not collectivisation.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: War is held a perennial ennobling feature of human life, not an effect of capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: The State's claim on individuals is total and its needs come first.

harm-principle.rationale: The State is an inwardly accepted discipline of the whole person, not a device limited to protecting a sphere of rights.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The Doctrine says individuals are accepted only so far as they coincide with the State and rights belong to the State.

conscription.rationale: The Doctrine glorifies war and duty to the nation, with military service as the core of the fighting spirit.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Exit from the national community is incompatible with a State all-embracing and obligations that bind individuals.

state-as-business.rationale: The State is a spiritual and ethical entity, not a business serving customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: The Doctrine's liberty is liberty of the State and individual within it, which is neither side of the statement.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed; mystics did not frame it this way.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The mystical wing was influenced by racial thinkers like Evola, but Italian doctrine treated race as spiritual; the genetic claim was not central.

organic-representation.rationale: The Doctrine describes individuals grouped by interests and economic activities within corporations that coordinate them in the State.

total-state.rationale: The Doctrine states that the Fascist State is totalitarian and interprets and potentiates the whole life of a people.

national-rebirth.rationale: The Doctrine presents Fascism as a spiritual revolt against decadent materialist ideas and a revival of sacred principles.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The Doctrine says a nation is a living entity only if it expands its power beyond frontiers.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The School demanded absolute personal loyalty to the Duce, though this was modern party loyalty, not feudal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Feudal bondage is not part of the Doctrine; its corporative ethos binds all to the State, not to lords.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Mystics held doctrine true by faith and tradition rather than neutral reason, which partially resembles this, though the claim is a postmodern one.

universal-morality.rationale: The Doctrine denies universals divorced from the nation, and mystics ground belief in faith and sentiment, not reason.

single-common-good.rationale: The State is a unity of all values expressing one conscience and one will, not balancing competing interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Radical right mystics of the Iron Guard type were antisemitic; Italian Fascism was mixed before 1938, so low confidence.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Neither the Doctrine nor the mystics discuss diaspora citizenship; Fascist Italy courted emigrant communities, but no principle decides it.

revive-national-language.rationale: Italian was already national; the Doctrine is silent on language revival.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Fascism rejects democratic mass rule and class bodies; firms are coordinated from above through the State.

school-vouchers.rationale: The Doctrine says the State educates and shapes the spirit, so education is not left to parental choice.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Public finance never appears in the mystics' writings, and the regime ran deficits for armaments and empire, so nothing is stated either way.

economic-freedom.rationale: The Doctrine says Fascism is opposed to liberalism in both the political and economic spheres.

rule-by-example.rationale: The mystics held the Duce and heroic martyrs as moral examples demanding devotion, though the regime also relied on force and law.

national-self-determination.rationale: The Doctrine grants independence to nations with a self-conscious will expressed in a State, which they must earn by strength.

force-without-un.rationale: The Doctrine calls internationalist superstructures useless and holds force a sign of a living state.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Fascist mysticism rests on fideism, with doctrine taken on faith and sentiment rather than reason.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare was for members of the national community in which the State's duty lies.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The Doctrine glorifies work and duty, so conditional welfare fits, though specific policy was not discussed.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Doctrine rejects class struggle and has the corporative system harmonise classes in the State.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The Doctrine values tradition and culture in all forms as high-value forces and the State respects them.

dominated-front.rationale: Italy saw itself as a proletarian nation against plutocracies, but the mystics took no recorded position on a common front.

workers-nation.rationale: The Doctrine denies class internationalism and makes workers part of the nation's State.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Doctrine's differentiation and rank, and the regime's cult of virility, favour separate roles for men and women.

ban-interest.rationale: Not a Fascist demand; the Iron Guard and Evola-type circles condemned usury but the Italian state kept banking.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The regime imposed racial laws in 1938; mystics such as Evola endorsed them, but the Doctrine says Fascism is not about race and views differ.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Doctrine denies the Marxist view and treats the State as an ethical, spiritual entity above classes.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Autarkic strength implies exploiting domestic resources; not discussed by mystics.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The Doctrine shapes a people through State education into one will and conscience, implying assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: Radical right mystics like the Iron Guard saw conspiracies, but replacement theory is a later notion and not documented for Italian mystics.

proportional-representation.rationale: The Doctrine rejects party parliamentary democracy and mass counting of votes.

national-mission.rationale: The Doctrine says individuals and generations are bound by a moral law with a mission and tradition.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Fascists affirm male leadership and hierarchy as natural order and would reject the claim of oppression.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Fascism attacks liberal parliamentary politicians as corrupt, though it would exempt its own leadership.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Nazi-style eugenics was not central to the Italian mystics; the Iron Guard and Evola defined the new man spiritually.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The State defends its fallen and martyrs and does not accept judgement of its forces by outside standards.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Doctrine says the State's functions cannot be limited to enforcing order and keeping peace.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The regime's 1938 laws discouraged it, and Evola-type thinkers favoured spiritual racial purity, but the Doctrine rejects race as basis.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Doctrine rejects political equalitarianism, affirming differentiation and rank.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Fascism rejects Marxian socialism wholly and does not deal with its internal debates.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The Doctrine glorifies empire and colonial expansion as proof of vitality.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The State and Catholic Church were reconciled in Italy; the mystics did not address personal law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; the regime protected Catholicism as the religion of Italians.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not a Fascist concern; no basis for it in the Doctrine.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The Doctrine says the State protects religion, and the regime placed Catholic instruction in schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The Doctrine holds the State should be strong and all-embracing; the claim is Marxist, so only partial fit.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Doctrine denies popular consent as source of authority; the State creates the nation and its will.

trade-surplus.rationale: Autarky and national strength imply surplus exporting, though not a stated mystic theme.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The Doctrine says Fascism rejects pacifism and finds nobility in war and conquest.

population-transfer.rationale: Radical right mystics were hostile to minorities, but Italian mystics left it unaddressed.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The Doctrine says war alone keys up all human energies and sets the seal of nobility on peoples.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The regime banned all other parties and holds nothing outside the State, though it was itself the extremist party.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Liberty is only the liberty of the State and of the individual within it; arbitrary power by the Duce is accepted.

separated-powers.rationale: The Doctrine says the State is a single unity, with no groups outside it.

vanguard-party.rationale: The School trained Fascist elites to lead the masses in devotion, much like a vanguard, though an elite of faith not class.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Fascism claims to look after the nation as a whole, with no primacy given to a class.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure was no concern of the school; the Doctrine gives no principle on selling state-owned homes.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The Doctrine rejects trade unionism as a class weapon outside the State and the regime banned strikes.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The regime's population policy sought more births and denied that growth is a problem.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The Doctrine wants a people unified as one conscience and one will, implying that diversity weakens it.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Authority rests on the few and the leader, not equality of citizens.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The totalitarian State holds all protections subordinate to its needs, and the regime enacted special laws against enemies.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The regime used price controls in autarky; inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: The totalitarian state shapes the whole of culture and the mystics formed the minds of believers through party schooling.

party-commands-army.rationale: The regime merged the party's militia (MVSN) with state structures, and loyalty is to the Duce, but the monarchy kept the army.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The nation as historical people favours restrictive naturalisation, inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Egalitarian pay of officials is alien to rank and differentiation.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The School demanded absolute loyalty to the Duce and the doctrine, with devotion and obedience.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The Doctrine rejects internationalistic superstructures and values national sovereignty.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The Duce commanded the party and held the war ministries, and the mystics demanded loyalty to him.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Giani's circle sought good relations with bishops but did not address church governance.

clerical-rule.rationale: The School asserted the Fascist State and the Duce's doctrine, not clergy, as the highest authority.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The Doctrine requires sacrifice for the nation in war; defeatism is cowardly.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The totalitarian State shapes culture to moral ends and the regime censored art.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The Duce was to rule indefinitely as infallible leader.

recall-officials.rationale: Authority flows from the leader downward, not from voters.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Italy pursued alliances like the Axis, and the Doctrine favours expansion.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Banning landlords is a radical levelling scheme foreign to a regime that kept private property under State direction; inferred, not discussed.

people-in-arms.rationale: The Doctrine's cult of the fighting spirit and the regime's militarised youth and militia favoured an armed nation, but alongside a regular army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The Iron Guard glorified peasant life as the spiritual core, and the Fascist regime promoted ruralism.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The Doctrine prizes expansion, and irredentism was part of Italian nationalism.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The mystics relied on youth and faith over intellectualism, yet were themselves a school of educated cadres.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The Doctrine asserts hierarchy and mission of the nation and empire as marks of higher civilisation.

death-penalty.rationale: The State is severe and the regime restored the death penalty for crimes against it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not the State's aim; the Doctrine's moral education emphasises duty and austerity.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not a Fascist concern; religious teaching was in state schools but creationism was not an issue.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The austere, serious and religious ethos of the Doctrine and regime censorship favour it.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The nation as a people historically perpetuating itself fits descent, though the Doctrine downplays race.

minority-language-support.rationale: The regime suppressed minority languages in Fascist Italianisation, and the State stands for one will.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The State's authority is all-embracing and permits no exemption outside it.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The Doctrine is anti-individualistic, demanding conformity of the whole person to State discipline.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The mystics wrote nothing on international debt; Fascist nationalism resents foreign creditors but also respects state obligations.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not addressed by mystics; the corporate state used a mixed answer.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The Doctrine rejects democracy by majority; constitutions are changed by the regime.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The State may restrain liberty in the name of national development, as the corporate state did.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The Doctrine denies universal duties across nations; neighbor means something concrete.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Not discussed in the 1930s, inferred from the nation's will to power and rejection of dependence.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The Duce's authority rests on faith in the leader, not popular election.

central-bank-independence.rationale: An all-embracing State would not accept independence of institutions from its direction.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The Doctrine holds that nations that expand are alive and giving land up is weakness.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The State subordinates private property to the national interest.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Fascists deny Marxist categories altogether, so this isn't theirs.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk lay outside the interwar mystics' horizon, and the Doctrine gives no guidance.

collective-defense.rationale: The regime signed the Pact of Steel; the Doctrine envisages power beyond frontiers, though it distrusts League superstructures.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The Doctrine's expansion thesis rejects this; Fascist Italy annexed territories by force.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Mystics wanted a Catholic Fascist loyal to the State first, though the regime concluded the Concordat with the Church.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The Duce was to be the infallible head of the party and nation, not above party.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The State is a single unity and force is acceptable.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The Doctrine's centralised State leaves no autonomy for different systems.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The School taught the Duce as infallible and an object of faith, though Italian Fascism did not claim divine descent.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax design was not a theme of the Doctrine or the mystics, so there is no basis for a position.

character-from-environment.rationale: The Doctrine ascribes spiritual formation to a will and mission through education, not an environmental determinism; it stresses the will and spirit.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Duce's word was absolute truth for Fascists; the Doctrine says the State is above law's limits.

space-expansion.rationale: Space was not on the interwar agenda; the Doctrine's worship of expansion could be stretched to it, but no source does so.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The Doctrine says power is of one will, not mixed.

leader-cult.rationale: The School of Fascist Mysticism was founded to cultivate devotion to the infallible Duce.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not covered; the traditionalist family ethos would favour maternal care but no source states it.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The Doctrine rejects Marxism wholesale, so debates on class struggle within socialism are outside its terms; it would disagree with the premise.

land-redistribution.rationale: The regime chose to protect landlords after the early radical Fasci programme; no mystical view.

refugee-return.rationale: The Doctrine and the school say nothing on refugees, and the regime's own expulsion of minorities cuts against a firm yes.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The Doctrine's expansion and irredentism, and Italian claims to Dalmatia or Nice, fit.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Not addressed by mystics; the Church's role is left separate.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not a Fascist demand and alien to Catholic Italy.

common-currency.rationale: The Doctrine rejects internationalistic superstructures that limit sovereignty.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Evola-circle imperial ideas hint at it, but Italian mystics stayed national.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The regime suppressed minority institutions and the State admits no groups outside.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Nothing in the mystics addresses minority strategy of this kind; antisemitic circles around Evola would reject it, Italian ones were silent.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The Doctrine rejects materialism and the economic interpretation of history in favour of spirit.

ban-cartels.rationale: The corporative state organised producers into corporations and did not break them up.

no-bailouts.rationale: The State would rescue firms for the nation's strength (e.g. IRI); inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The Doctrine denies majority rule but the State overrides courts.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarky was Fascism's declared aim, though the mystics left economics to others.

moral-incentives.rationale: The Doctrine exalts duty, sacrifice and spiritual motives over material pleasure and pay.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The squadrists' action created the revolution as the Doctrine tells it.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Evola's strand defends aristocracy, and the regime kept the monarchy, though Fascism also claimed a meritocratic elite.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The Doctrine values tradition and the nation's mission in history, and the regime taught history for nation building.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Doctrine glorifies empire and the regime justified conquest in Ethiopia as civilising.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Doctrine says Fascist education moulds the will and the school system prepares spiritual loyalty to the nation.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Affirmative action was unknown to the school; its rejection of egalitarianism is general rather than aimed at preferences.

public-money-creation.rationale: The mystics are silent on monetary mechanics, and the Doctrine says only that the State directs economic life.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The Doctrine does not predict capitalist collapse; capitalism is tolerated within the corporative frame.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Fascism claimed Roman imperial heritage, and Evola called for an imperial Roman revival.

delink-world-market.rationale: Autarky resembles it but is a rich nation's policy.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist notion that Fascism rejects in favour of national unity.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The State's interest in the nation limits private freedom of association.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Doctrine rejects individual rights above the State.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not addressed; Italy was bitter about Versailles, but the claim concerns colonised peoples.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Doctrine rejects election, and authority comes from the leader and State.

minority-veto.rationale: The Doctrine's one will and discipline reject minority vetoes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The School demanded absolute loyalty to the Duce.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics does not appear in the Doctrine or the school's writings.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not discussed by the mystics or in the Doctrine.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The Doctrine's duty of the powerful to others and the nation fits, with elites bound to serve.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The Doctrine says life is duty and conquest, lived above all for others.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Fascism used mass culture for mobilisation, but critiques of it as pacifying are not its own.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian claim that Fascism neither adopts nor denies.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Italian fascism claimed to be a proletarian nation against plutocracies, which resembles it somewhat, but mystics gave no view.

native-born-offices.rationale: The nation-as-people theme implies this, though it was not stated.

party-own-road.rationale: A communist question to which Fascism has no answer.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The Doctrine wants nations to prove their will and autarky is its aim.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Italian irredentism and the Doctrine's expansion thesis demand regaining claimed lands.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; the colonial empire contradicts it.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Fascists reject being outlawed and treat liberalism and democracy as exhausted.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Fascists deny equivalence and called communism a resolute negation.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: American history lay outside the Italian mystics' concerns, and no source gives a position.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The Doctrine honours its heroes and martyrs and tradition.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The mystics addressed duty and virility, not welfare gaps between the sexes; no stated position.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence policy is not discussed by the Doctrine or the school.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The Doctrine says Fascism is a form for its time and nation and denies universal liberal models.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The Doctrine's fighting spirit and the regime's militarism fit a political role for the armed forces.

paid-care-work.rationale: The regime did not treat housework as paid labour and glorified motherhood as duty.

filial-duty.rationale: The Doctrine binds generations by moral law and respect for tradition.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not a mystical theme; Fascism favoured loyalty and the Duce's choice.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Autarky and national control of strategic industry fit.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The regime upheld Catholic marriage and Italy had no divorce.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Authority flows from above, not through delegates bound by voters.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The corporative state favoured collective social insurance.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The State claims no such tenure; the regime kept private property.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The Doctrine rejects parliamentary democracy and the regime's parliament was a corporative chamber.

single-official-language.rationale: The regime forced Italianisation, and the State wills one conscience.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Nationalist autarky implies it but is not stated.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The Doctrine denies political equalitarianism and affirms rank, so remedies for unequal outcomes between groups are rejected in principle.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The Doctrine condemns the instinct of selfish momentary pleasure and materialism.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The regime backed foreign movements such as the Ustasha, but mystics did not address it.

corporate-influence.rationale: Fascism subordinates business to the State but isn't hostile to business.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The totalitarian State tolerates no outside influence.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The Doctrine says the population policy of the regime is a consequence of its premises.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local property restrictions are not addressed; the Fascist state centralised authority, which cuts against local powers, but no source decides it.

job-guarantee.rationale: The regime stressed work as duty but no guarantee was promised by the mystics.

democratic-peace.rationale: The Doctrine rejects democracy and perpetual peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The State is inwardly accepted rule of conduct and loyalty to the Duce is absolute.

non-intervention.rationale: The Doctrine values power beyond frontiers; intervention by a strong state is its norm.

industrial-unions.rationale: The corporations were organised by sector, but mystics took no position.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The Iron Guard and Evola's circle blamed a Jewish conspiracy, but the Italian Fascist mystics did less so before 1938.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage and family are pillars of the regime's population policy.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The totalitarian State shapes information and holds secrets.

local-production.rationale: Autarky favours national, not local, production.

informal-organisation.rationale: Fascism favoured disciplined, hierarchical organisation under the party.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The Doctrine rejects internationalist superstructures and puts the national State supreme.

religious-nation.rationale: Mystics sought a political-religious faith in the nation but Catholicism was respected as the religion of Italians, while the Doctrine defines the nation as a people not a creed.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Not addressed; Fascism wanted Italy to be the leading power.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The Doctrine's centralised, all-embracing State directs resources for the whole nation, which excludes regional fiscal autonomy.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The Doctrine does not use the means-of-production distinction; private possessions were safe in the regime, but this is not stated.

defeat-communism.rationale: The Doctrine calls Fascism the resolute negation of Marxian socialism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Service delivery models are not discussed by the mystics; the corporative state mixed public and private bodies in practice.

religion-illusion.rationale: The Doctrine sees life as religious and spiritual and condemns materialism.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The Doctrine is ambivalent, accepting private enterprise under the State while condemning materialism.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Fascism denies equalitarian claims and Marxist economic readings.

socialized-care.rationale: The regime made the family the base of society.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The regime campaigned against foreign words as part of Italianisation.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations are not discussed, and the Doctrine makes the State's will supreme, leaving the question open.

cooperative-communities.rationale: No groups outside the State, and the regime was nationally centralised.

majority-settlement.rationale: The regime settled Italians in South Tyrol and elsewhere.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The Doctrine rejects both liberalism and Marxian socialism for a third corporative order.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The Doctrine's imperial heritage claims Roman lands.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Evola never clearly acknowledged the Holocaust, but Italian mystics did not take up the question.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Italy did not criminalise it but the ethos was hostile; mystics took no recorded position.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Doctrine says no individuals or groups outside the State, and the regime banned other parties.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Not addressed beyond the Church-State accommodation.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Fascist empire aimed at Italian settlement and national benefit.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: The question concerns Islamic law and falls outside an Italian Catholic-national mysticism; no position is documented.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The mystics held the Duce's doctrine as the ruling faith and not clerical legitimacy.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The Doctrine rejects rule by the majority and holds that the State, not citizens' direct decisions, expresses the nation's will.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The framework assumes egalitarian ends that the Doctrine rejects as an absurd lie, so adherents reject its premise.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The traditional moral order and the cult of virility leave no room for it; inferred from the regime's moral order.

assisted-dying.rationale: The Doctrine rejects suicide as cowardly and affirms life as duty.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The Doctrine claims to be beyond left and right yet defines itself against liberalism and socialism.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist notion, though Fascism claimed to dignify labour in corporations.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Mystics wanted politics given religious force but the Duce, not God, was the object; the Church disputed the term.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The Concordat era had priests and crucifixes in state institutions, but the mystics never discussed dress codes.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: A modern workplace-law issue absent from the mystics' world; no position can be documented.

social-market-economy.rationale: The regime's third way was corporative not liberal-social.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The Doctrine calls pacifism cowardly renunciation and says war sets the seal of nobility on peoples, so abolishing armies is the opposite of its creed.

rich-first.rationale: The Doctrine accepts hierarchy and differentiation, though growth theory is absent.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The Doctrine's expansionist aims led the regime to join the Axis.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The Duce was a charismatic leader chosen by destiny, not succession by blood.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Monetary reform is not in the mystics' writings; the Iron Guard condemned finance, but no source gives the Italian view.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: National sovereignty over economic policy fits, though not stated.

property-franchise.rationale: The regime abolished voting rather than restricting it by property.

domination-women-nature.rationale: An ecofeminist claim opposed to the traditional, virile ethos.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept not accepted, though the critique of materialism is shared in part.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Fascism controlled the press, but the claim is from the left.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The Duce's word was absolute truth and the State above rules.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Doctrine rejects race as basis, though later racial laws and Evola-type circles went further.

online-participation.rationale: Not applicable; mass participation by internet runs against hierarchy.

open-government-data.rationale: A totalitarian State that shapes information and demands faith in its leader would reject radical transparency.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Not addressed; 1938 laws restricted marriage to Jews.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Iron Guard circles did; Italian mystics left it.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Rule by quality not quantity and rejects mass deliberation.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The mystics treated tradition and faith as fixed truths.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The Doctrine's liberty is the State's and wealth is subordinated to the nation.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The warrior ethos of the Doctrine and Evola's hypermasculine ideal reject it; inferred.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Doctrine's conception of life is religious and the State protects religion.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The State is authority and power, and this is anathema.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The State is one will and does not share power among communities.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The State claims the whole life of the people, though charity was part of the Catholic order.

term-limits.rationale: The leader rules indefinitely and without limit.

vote-delegation.rationale: Mass voting is rejected altogether by the Doctrine, so delegated voting schemes are rejected too.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The Doctrine rejects utopian progress but glorifies heroic risk; extinction risk is not discussed.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The traditionalist order assigns distinct roles.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The traditional family holds male headship in the regime's ethos.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The nation is a historical people and voting rights are denied even to citizens.

rent-control.rationale: Rent policy is not addressed by the mystics; the regime did freeze rents at times for social peace, but no source ties this to the doctrine.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed, and the corporative state protected property.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The Doctrine's education and discipline shaped youth, and the regime ran the Opera Nazionale Balilla and the School trained young Fascist leaders.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nuclear weapons postdate the mystics, and the Doctrine's national sovereignty gives no clear answer.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: National sovereignty and will to power favour it, though inferred.

recognise-genocide.rationale: The Doctrine denies guilt for acts of war and empire, but the question was not discussed.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The Doctrine glorifies work and duty as the basis of citizenship in the corporative state.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The Doctrine holds that life is duty and conquest, and rejects pacifism.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The Doctrine says a people is historically perpetuating itself, and Fascism claims Roman continuity.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The traditional view treats sex as natural and fixed.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: The Doctrine's differentiated roles assume fixed categories.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The Doctrine points to Fascism's fallen heroes and martyrs, and the School of Fascist Mysticism centred on a cult of the fallen.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The School of Fascist Mysticism held Fascism to be a faith and mythology, and politics a spiritual battle demanding devotion.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Fascist Italy promoted its culture among emigrants, but the mystics did not state a view on homelands and diasporas.

culture-before-state.rationale: The Doctrine says the State creates the nation, though mystics saw spiritual formation as preceding action.

god-not-male.rationale: The religious frame is Catholic and traditionalist.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: The traditional hierarchy of the mystics and Evola's subordination of women reject judging religion by feminist standards.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The regime's nationalism implies this, and the 1938 laws removed Jews from the economy.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The Doctrine's nation as one will fits unified territory.

independent-unions.rationale: The Doctrine says no groups outside the State and unions are only within the corporation.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The Doctrine rejects Marxian socialism wholesale.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The corporative state mixed public and private ownership and mystics gave no view on local utilities.

second-chamber.rationale: The regime replaced the Senate and Chamber with a corporative chamber but mystics gave no view.

municipal-property.rationale: The State is the unity of all values and the regime centralised.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The Doctrine's single, all-embracing State leaves no room for federated municipalities that administer but do not govern.

family-wage.rationale: The regime's population policy and corporations supported family allowances.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Medical regulation is not addressed by the mystics.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Longevity research lies outside the mystics' concerns; their spiritual emphasis on sacrifice gives no clear answer.

anonymous-payments.rationale: A State that tolerates nothing outside it would not allow it.

online-anonymity.rationale: A totalitarian State that tolerates no group outside its discipline would not allow anonymous political activity.

person-over-state.rationale: The Doctrine accepts the individual only so far as his interests coincide with the State's.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The Doctrine says the conception is spiritual and Fascism sees life as more than material.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: A centralised State can withdraw local powers.

gm-crops.rationale: Agricultural biotechnology postdates the mystics; the regime's agrarian rhetoric gives no answer.

dense-cities.rationale: The regime was anti-urban and prized the countryside.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The Doctrine says the nation is not a race, but Evola-type and later racial theorists held groups have interests; adherents split.

racial-pride.rationale: Spiritual race and pride in ancestry feature in Evola-type thought, though the Doctrine says not a race.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The Doctrine rejects pacifism and asserts expansion and power beyond frontiers.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The Doctrine rejects political equalitarianism and affirms differentiation and rank, and the regime kept women out of leadership.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The Doctrine sees power beyond frontiers as proof of a living state, so a dominant state policing its bloc fits; not stated by mystics.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Italian mystics were concerned with Catholic Italy and its own empire; no documented view on Islam and the West.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism grounds the nation in a spiritual will and in the State that creates it, not in language alone; inferred from that, as the mystics did not address language.

communal-electorates.rationale: The Doctrine rejects universal suffrage and party representation in favour of a single totalitarian State, so separate religious electorates have no place.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Fascist rhetoric cast Italy as a proletarian nation encircled by plutocratic powers; inferred, as the mystics wrote little on this specific claim.

free-public-college.rationale: The mystics left education policy aside beyond training a Fascist elite, and the sources do not say whether tuition should be free.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred from the corporative State's command over economic life through directives, not taxes, and its disregard for environmental questions.

future-generations.rationale: The Doctrine speaks of duty to the nation's continuity across generations, but stewardship of the Earth was no theme; adherents' view is unclear.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Fascism prized martial, virile values and confined women to the home; inferred from the Doctrine's glorification of war, with Evola's fringe giving a similar view of women.

arms-reduction.rationale: The Doctrine states that only war brings human energy to its highest tension and rejects perpetual peace as cowardice.

open-diplomacy.rationale: The totalitarian State's leader-centred foreign policy implies secrecy; inferred, since the mystics did not discuss treaty publicity.

capital-controls.rationale: The corporative State subordinates economic activity to national ends, so state control of capital movements fits; inferred, as the mystics wrote little on economics.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The Doctrine places all organised force under the totalitarian State, and the regime folded squadrist units into a state militia; inferred agreement, though not a mystics' theme.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The Doctrine holds that war raises human energy to its highest tension and ennobles those who face it, so refusing to fight is condemned.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The corporative system fixed collective labour contracts through state-recognised syndicates, but outside free union bargaining; mild agreement inferred.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Not discussed by the mystics or the Doctrine; no clear position follows.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The Doctrine subordinates economics to the State's will, so legal limits on the state's borrowing are inferred to be disliked.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Fascism cast Italy as a proletarian nation against plutocratic powers, which suggests support for revising international economic rules, though for national ends.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Fascism took over and used the existing state, making it totalitarian rather than destroying it, so disagreement is inferred.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The Doctrine demands a single corporative order within an all-embracing State, with no room for free economic experiment.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not discussed; the mystics left economics aside.

sacred-nation.rationale: The Doctrine describes the nation as a spiritual and ethical reality that outlasts individuals and gives them a higher life, and the School of Mysticism made this a faith.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not discussed and no doctrinal basis either way.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The Doctrine stresses the unity of the nation under the State rather than exploitation between regions; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The Doctrine rejects natural rights and individualist dignity, and the mystics wanted to forge a new type of man; a fixed human nature as basis for rights is inferred to be rejected.

public-service-media.rationale: The regime ran broadcasting as an arm of the State and propaganda, so independence from government control is inferred to be rejected.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The mystics treated Fascism itself as a faith needing its own cult, and Fascism's Catholic accommodation stopped short of endorsing a common truth in all religions; inferred.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from the corporative state's direction of the economy and the regime's 'battle for grain'; the mystics themselves left economics aside.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Doctrine's glorification of power, war and national strength, which rules out disarming alone.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Doctrine rejects class politics and socialism and sets the single party and corporations above class, so an independent workers' party is excluded.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not discussed by the mystics; the totalitarian state could ban it, but the sources do not settle the point.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from Fascism's subordination of women to family and nation; the sources give no inheritance position.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; the regime promoted Italian but nothing here fixes a view on regional names.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from the Doctrine's all-embracing State, which regulates by authority rather than leaving matters to private suits.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from the Doctrine's single sovereign State above all groups, leaving no separate chiefly role in lawmaking.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the Doctrine's view that the State stands above individuals and may require sacrifice from them.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the regime's authoritarian justice and the Doctrine's demand for order under the State.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from the Doctrine's demand that all within the State's reach conform to the nation's spiritual unity.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from the Doctrine: workers were organised in state-controlled corporations, so membership was compulsory under the regime.

voter-id.rationale: Elections were abolished and the mystics did not address voter ID, so the issue is outside the doctrine (inferred).

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred: Fascism put the State above all and made its own creed a civic religion, so it would not accept legal equality between interpretations.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism rejects democracy as rule by numbers and holds that legitimacy comes from the State and the leader, not elections.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the regime's traditional, pro-natalist morality, which the mystics' cult of sacrifice and discipline reinforced.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the totalitarian State claiming control over all of national life, with order and unity above individual liberty.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from corporative economics and a paternalist state, which would not replace welfare with individual cash payments.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred from the regime's view of women's role in family and nation; Fascist Italy gave women only limited local votes before abolishing local elections.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from the mystics' own religion of Fascism, which valued faith and held that religion supports sacrifice and social order.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred: the mystics spoke of spiritual and national race, and the regime later adopted biological racism, so they did not see race as a mere construct.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from the regime's pro-natalism and its own women's organisations under party control, not equality agencies.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the Doctrine's State above individuals: property is held at the State's pleasure, not as a natural right of first claimants.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: The Doctrine rejects internationalism and pacifism and glorifies war and national sovereignty, so leaders answering to courts above the nation is alien to it.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The mystics' faith rested on myth and devotion to the Duce rather than on scriptural literalism, and they clashed with the Church; inferred from this fideism.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the Doctrine's totalitarian State and traditional sex roles; guaranteed gender equality in group self-rule has no place in it.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The Doctrine is explicitly anti-socialist and rejects Marxist collectivism, so defending a socialist planned state is opposed.

indirect-election.rationale: The Doctrine rejects universal suffrage and democracy in favour of hierarchy and corporative representation built from the top down.

national-church-status.rationale: The regime gave Catholicism special status, but the mystics' own relation to the Church was disputed, so this is inferred and contested.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The Doctrine's single totalitarian State above all groups leaves no room for ethnic territorial autonomy.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: The Doctrine rejects counting heads as the source of right and prizes nationhood, force and expansion over local votes.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred: the movement glorified empire and had no doctrine of post-colonial borders, so it would reject independence rather than endorse its borders.

simple-living.rationale: The Doctrine rejects the comfortable life and happiness-seeking in favour of sacrifice, struggle and austerity, which the mystics cultivated.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred: the regime encouraged Italian settlement in its colonies and prized expansion, so limiting settlers would be opposed.

equal-conscription.rationale: The Doctrine holds that war is to man what maternity is to woman, assigning military duty to men only.

missingStatements.text: Politics should be founded on faith in a doctrine accepted without rational proof.
missingStatements.rationale: The School of Fascist Mysticism defined mysticism as belief held through tradition or sentiment and demanded unquestioning faith in the Duce's doctrine.

missingStatements.text: A political movement should honour those who died for it as heroes whose example binds the living.
missingStatements.rationale: The Doctrine points to Fascism's fallen heroes and martyrs, and the School made their cult a training tool; the Iron Guard did the same.

missingStatements.text: Politics should aim to create a new kind of person through spiritual discipline and sacrifice.
missingStatements.rationale: The Doctrine speaks of a higher life founded on duty and self-sacrifice, and the Iron Guard's new man was defined spiritually through self-purification.

notes: Many answers are inferred from the Doctrine and the regime because the mystics wrote on faith and devotion, not policy. Evola's pagan Traditionalism and the Iron Guard's Orthodox mysticism would differ on religion, race and hierarchy. I did not open the Wikipedia article for Niccolo Giani; the link is used only as a figure's page.
